checks.why: the test reaches the change only through a callable handed over as a value. That is its own kind of evidence and it used to be reported as `one of a set` — a claim that the engine resolved the call to a sound target set, which is the one thing a hand-off is not. The tier fell through CERT_UP's default, which was the third most certain rung of ten (#1123)
and the label is explained where it is used, because a reader cannot rank evidence whose name is never defined
want: [registered] is a callable handed over as a value

checks.why: the rung is BELOW `one of a set` and above the name matches: a hand-off is a real engine edge, so `by name` understates it, and it is not a resolution, so `one of a set` overstates it

the DIRECT layer said [resolved] and 'calls it' for the same hand-off. Both dependents here pass or invoke `normalise` as a value and neither calls it; the label came from `'one of a set' if tier == 'multi_inferred' else 'resolved'`, a binary test standing in for an eleven-value vocabulary (#1131)
